title: Leclere–Morier-Genoud trace unimodality conjecture
statement: Let $c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_k$ be integers, and let $M_q(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_k)$ be the associated matrix in $\mathrm{PSL}_q(2,\mathbb{Z})$. **Leclere–Morier-Genoud trace unimodality conjecture.** For any sequence $c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_k$ of integers, the trace $\mathrm{tr}(M_q(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_k))$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ with unimodal coefficients. The paper states this conjecture as an analogue of the unimodality question for circular rank polynomials, but later gives evidence that the cited conjecture does not hold.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05517

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2022). “This implies in particular that Conjecture does not hold, but one can apply the results from Theorem to characterize large families where we have unimodality.”
source_name: Ezgi Kantarcı Oğuz, “Oriented posets, Rank Matrices and q-deformed Markov Numbers”, arXiv:2206.05517 (2024).
